clue.text: Horrified scallywag has turned to bottle

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold inside, so the answer sits within the run of letters scallywag has turned

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked to find that a rascal has taken to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bottle' looks like drinking, but it signals the answer held inside 'scallywAG HAS Turned'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone filled with horror and dismay is aghast.

indicators.note: in a down answer, the rearranged letters come below the P
something buckled is bent out of shape, so the letters of sailor are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaman cracks under stress.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' puts the anagram of SAILOR below P.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris is the Pole Star, the bright star used by navigators to find north.

clue.text: One to be out all night? Most unlikely!

definitions.text: One to be out all night? Most unlikely!

parts.words: One to be out all night? Most unlikely!
parts.note: being out can mean being unconscious; a person who cannot sleep is the last one to be out cold all night

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that a stay-at-home type would party all night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' reads as out on the town, but here it means out cold, asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepless person lies awake rather than spending the night out cold, which is the cryptic twist.

clue.text: Each to secure three points in addition

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the word for each holds the three points

parts.note: all can mean each, as in a score of two all
S, W and E are three points of the compass: south, west, east

explanation.surface: Each team grabs three points on top of what it already had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three points' sounds like a football win but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning also or besides, the same as in addition.

clue.text: Sale items from two Biblical figures

parts.note: the first figure is Job, the patient man tested by God in the Old Testament
the second figure is Lot, Abraham's nephew who fled Sodom

explanation.surface: Auction lots are drawn from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a mixed bundle of goods bought or sold together at auction.

parts.note: a huge plane flying between countries, with tremendous for jumbo and winger for a winged aircraft

explanation.surface: It sounds like praise for a wide player on a national football team.
explanation.walkthrough: A winger is a football player, but here it means anything with wings: a big airliner.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wide-bodied airliner such as the Boeing 747 used on long international routes.

clue.text: Bold self-confidence seen in orchestra section

definitions.meaning: cheek or nerve, as in having the ... neck to ask
the trumpets, trombones and horns of an orchestra

explanation.surface: A brash confidence shows among the players of an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for both impudent nerve and the metal wind instruments of an orchestra.

parts.note: something done is over, finished
a look is a style or fashion

explanation.surface: Someone is declared to be no longer in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a title for a woman, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to notice something is to miss it, a plain synonym.

indicators.note: poor here means in a bad way, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An owner cries out in sympathy at a pet's injured snout.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise: 'My!' and 'Goodness!' are interchangeable.

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a rascal

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: ailed means was troubled or unwell; said aloud it gives the ending of the answer

explanation.surface: A worried rogue finds himself stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierced through and held fast on a spike, which is to be stuck in a literal way.

clue.text: Mission appears in article by the French medic

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
la is French for the (feminine)
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A mission is staffed by a French doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was a Spanish mission in Texas, famous for its siege in 1836.

parts.note: a lemon is a citrus fruit
sole means only, as in sole survivor

explanation.surface: Someone eats nothing but seafood and fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish of European waters, popular in restaurants.

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A shifty person comes from some other place.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake-like fish notoriously hard to grip, so a slippery creature.

clue.text: Muddle involving right one in complex romantic situation?

indicators.note: involving here means wrapping around, so the muddle surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a tangle is a muddle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A messy love affair is described as a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A love triangle: three people romantically entangled, a complex situation.

clue.text: Redo it with revision this boss may require?

definitions.text: Redo it with revision this boss may require?

indicators.note: revision means reworking, so the letters of the words before are reordered

explanation.surface: A newspaper chief orders a rewrite.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a picture of the person who demands rewrites.
explanation.definitionFit: The boss of a newspaper or book who sends copy back to be rewritten.

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hard-working military recruit died after his drills.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: committed and conscientious in work.

clue.text: Country songs sent up having limp content

indicators.note: content here means contents, so the word for limp is placed inside
in a down answer, sent up means read upwards, so the word is turned around

parts.note: airs are tunes or songs
lank hair is limp

explanation.surface: Country music is mocked for its feeble quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like a music genre, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An island nation in the Indian Ocean, formerly Ceylon.

definitions.meaning: in tennis, a serve the receiver cannot touch

explanation.surface: A tennis star delivers a serve that cannot be returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Two meanings: a winning serve in tennis and a highly skilled person.

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a scary film is really restful.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for both slang taking it easy and spine-chilling fright.

clue.text: Loathe having to leave hospital, being worried

indicators.note: the hospital letter is told to go, so it is removed

parts.note: to hate is to loathe
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A patient hates being discharged and frets about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of eat in the sense of bother, as in what's eating you?

parts.note: to reach a place is to arrive at it

explanation.surface: British tourists get to the Croatian city of Split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' reads as the Croatian port, but it means a break or rupture.
explanation.definitionFit: A break or gap, as in a breach in a wall, is a split.

definitions.meaning: a light brown colour, as of the skin after sun
to ... someone's hide is to thrash them, belt them

explanation.surface: It reads like a brown leather belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a colour of skin after sunbathing and a verb for giving a beating.

definitions.meaning: a player who begins the match, rather than coming off the bench
the first course of a meal

explanation.surface: There is nothing to replace a good first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a player in the opening line-up and the first course of a meal.

clue.text: Seaman to stray with the drink

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
to sin is to stray from what is right

explanation.surface: A sailor goes astray with a glass in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A potent green spirit flavoured with wormwood, a drink.

clue.text: Large bird goes after black dog

indicators.note: goes after means the bird comes later than the colour

parts.note: B is short for black, as on pencils
an eagle is a large bird of prey

explanation.surface: A big bird of prey chases a black dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hound bred for hunting hares, a breed of dog.

indicators.note: formed means shaped anew, so the letters of the mountain range are rearranged

explanation.surface: It reads like a geography note on how a mountain pass was formed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' looks like a mountain pass, but it is the verb, of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that goes by is said to pass; the verb is a synonym.

indicators.note: drunken means reeling and disordered, so the name's letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A tipsy Biondello, a servant in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew, lets slip his ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry or line of descent, especially of a pure-bred animal.

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis
nice means pleasant, delightful

explanation.surface: A lovely romance has been paused for now.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: plans put on hold are kept on ice.

clue.text: Trunk route located in China or Taiwan

indicators.note: located in means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A main road is found in one of two East Asian countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk route' sounds like a main road; here it is the body's main artery.
explanation.definitionFit: The main artery leaving the heart, the trunk route for blood through the body.

clue.text: Popular sauce is sent back, being dry

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: sent back means the words are turned around

parts.note: a dip is a sauce for dipping

explanation.surface: A trendy sauce is returned to the kitchen for being too dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and lacking flavour or interest, as dry prose is.

clue.text: Having no idea — not like our solvers!

definitions.meaning: solvers work from clues, so lacking them is the opposite of a solver

explanation.surface: A jibe at the ignorant, with a wink at the people doing the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant, and humorously without crossword hints, unlike those solving.

parts.note: bad means evil
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: A wicked impulse drives a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a dishonest or unpleasant person, like a rotter.
